milestone_summary: Fidelity Electronics released Chess Challenger, the first dedicated chess computer sold to the public.

quote: I alone of all men in the world have learnt how to collect the invisible vibrations of thought itself.
claim_description: A device that collects the electromagnetic 'vibrations' emitted by the human brain, i.e. thought detection.
concept_description: A machine that reads a person's specific thoughts, memories or images directly from their brain.
milestone_summary: ATR labs in Kyoto reconstructed 10x10-pixel images a person viewed from brain signals.

quote: Axel computed our route home on the electronic calculator
claim_description: A spacecraft's return route from Mars is computed on an onboard electronic calculator.
concept_description: A computer that calculates orbits, courses and engine burns and steers a spacecraft or ship along them.
milestone_summary: Same flight: first operational use of an onboard computer for orbital maneuvers on a crewed spacecraft.

quote: From this lens I shall pour upon the screen in a minute or two for you all to see, without doubt and in simple view, the thoughts of the man or woman on whom I shall place the cap.
claim_description: A 'Thought Spectroscope' that projects a person's thoughts as images onto a screen, like a magic lantern.
concept_description: A machine that writes down a person's thoughts as text, or shows their mental images or dreams on a screen.
milestone_summary: Chang and Makin at UCSF decoded spoken sentences from ECoG signals into text with 3% word error rate.

quote: Synaptic cells summed and integrated, cancelled and compared and with saucy assurance sent the findings on toward Cumulative.
claim_description: A computer with synaptic memory cells processes coded tapes through a multi-stage 'Cumulative' and 'Final Equate' pipeline to name a killer.
concept_name: Computer crime detection and predictive policing
concept_description: Computers that analyse police records and evidence to identify suspects or predict where crime will happen.
milestone_summary: The FBI's National Crime Information Center, a computerized national database of wanted persons and stolen property, was created.

quote: The cardex is chewing on the evidence, sir
claim_description: An automated card-index computer identifies a distant spacecraft from detector data.
concept_description: A machine that stores very large collections of records or documents and finds the items matching a query in seconds.
milestone_summary: Lockheed's interactive Dialog system (Roger Summit) was tested on NASA's STAR database at Ames in 1966, cutting searches from 14 hours to a few minutes; this became NASA RECON.

quote: Immediately the song came back at him through a little speaker, but in English—and with the unmistakable drawl of Rogers. "I conditioned it a few minutes ago with his voice,"
claim_description: A machine can instantly translate speech and reproduce it in a specific person's voice and accent after brief conditioning.
concept_description: A machine that generates spoken language with an artificial voice, such as a talking computer reading out answers.
milestone_summary: Telesensory Systems' Speech+ talking calculator for the blind, with a synthesized voice, was in use; the Kurzweil Reading Machine for the Blind (Votrax synthesizer) appeared in the same year.

quote: McGuire won't take orders from a woman.
claim_description: The ship's robot brain is built with an inhibition so it obeys only a male master's voice.
concept_description: A machine that recognizes spoken words and carries out spoken commands, such as voice-operated doors or computers.
milestone_summary: The Apricot Portable shipped with voice-command recognition (up to 4096 words, 64 in RAM at a time).

quote: The electronic say-who-please said just that. I answered clearly, "Wysten Turner," wondering if she'd given my name to the mechanism.
claim_description: Apartment doors have voice-activated electronic identification and entry systems.
concept_description: A machine that recognizes spoken words and carries out spoken commands, such as voice-operated doors or computers.
milestone_summary: The Apricot Portable shipped with voice-command recognition (up to 4096 words, 64 in RAM at a time).

quote: It is the one recreation that The Leader allows them. It's hard to explain exactly what it is, but you are carried away by it. It's something like a drug, yet it's mechanical.
claim_description: A mechanical device clamped to the temples gives users dream-like sensory experiences, serving as a drug-like entertainment machine.
concept_description: A machine that feeds a person's senses a computer-generated world convincing enough to feel real.
milestone_summary: Virtuality 1000SU VR systems launched in London in 1990 and sold to corporations (Ford, IBM, Mitsubishi, Olin) before the 1991 arcade version.

quote: It opened wide on the floor before him.
claim_description: The future case opens in response to a spoken command, a voice-activated lock.
concept_description: A machine that recognizes spoken words and carries out spoken commands, such as voice-operated doors or computers.
milestone_summary: The Apricot Portable shipped with voice-command recognition (up to 4096 words, 64 in RAM at a time).

quote: Illiterate business-machines, preparing Illiterate cards for same, filing recordings—always with the counsel, "When in doubt, consult a Literate."
claim_description: Business machines designed for non-readers using recorded speech and special cards, since the public has lost literacy.
